text:
Ryan Leonard played his 100th NHL game in Ottawa on Nov. 10, and RMNB marked it with Spencer Carbery recalling the early days. At 21, the eighth pick of 2023 is a regular in Washington's middle six, playing a little over 14 minutes a night with 11 points in 16 games.

His game is volume. Forty-one shots, many from distance (our comparisons put him alongside Jack Quinn and Arseny Gritsyuk), and five goals on 4.59 expected, so the finishing is about where it should be. The 5v5 shot share is fine at 52%, roughly level with the team.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.2 wins above replacement last season, mostly from offense, with a real knack for drawing penalties. The cost was defense: opponents got more chances with him on the ice (bottom 9% of forwards).

Among forwards drafted sixth to tenth since 2005, the median first full season is 0.40 points a game. Leonard is at about 0.69 this year. His ice time is the limit, not his production, and that is the number we'd watch.
headline: Leonard reaches 100 games still shooting from everywhere
